svg.title: What NanoVI does
svg.desc: NanoVI takes FASTQ files of full-length 16S rRNA Oxford Nanopore reads, one per sample. It keeps reads of 500 to 2,000 bases (fastplong), matches each read to the sequences of a 16S reference database built once from GTDB (minimap2), scores each match and estimates each species' share of the reads with NanoVI's Bayesian model, whose read score comes from Emu, and writes a species table per sample and one for the whole run, ready for R and phyloseq. Optional extras, switched on when asked for: groups of species that 16S cannot tell apart, abundances corrected for 16S copies per genome, the species each read was assigned to, and an HTML and PDF report.
